parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

BrightBrush makes eco-friendly toothbrushes from bamboo. Products are made in **batches**. The firm wants to cut defects and speed up output. Managers are thinking about moving to **flow production** and introducing **quality assurance** (checking during production) instead of relying on quality control at the end.

**Table 3.1 – Latest weekly production data**

| **Item** | **Value** |
|---|---|
| Total toothbrushes produced last week | 12 000 |
| Number of production workers | 48 |

Should BrightBrush use quality assurance or keep quality control as its main method? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Quality assurance, which is checking for quality during production **[K]**, finds faults early on the flow line **[Ap]**, reducing rework and scrap so productivity and business reputation are likely to improve as fewer faulty goods will reach the customer **[An]**
However, end-of-line checks** [K] **may be cheaper to start with for a small firm changing from batch to flow production** [Ap]**, avoiding heavy training costs and keeping production moving while processes stabilise and staff get used to the new system** [An]**
Overall, quality assurance should be the main method with simple end-line checks as a backup **[E]**. It fits the aim to cut defects and speed up output on a flow line, and savings from less rework offset training costs **[E]**

> 
>   - State two valid points relevant to the question, each with a different viewpoint → 2 K marks
>   - Apply each point clearly to the stimulus → 2 Ap marks
>   - Develop each point → 2 An marks
>   - Make a justified decision → 2 E marks
> - **Points might include**
> 
>   - Quality assurance
>   
>     - Finds faults during production; less rework/scrap on a flow line
>     - Builds quality culture; fewer customer complaints, better reputation
>     - Smoother throughput → higher labour productivity over time
>   - Quality control C
>   
>     - Cheaper/faster to start; minimal training while new line beds in
>     - Useful backstop to catch defects before dispatch
>   - Judgement
>   
>     - Training/time costs vs expected defect reduction
>     - Complexity of the new flow layout; staff skills and supervision
>     - Combining QA as main method with simple end-line QC checks

parts.problem_md: **Explain four** reasons why a business should maintain high quality standards.
parts.solution_md:
Maintaining high quality standards helps prevent customer complaints and negative reviews **[K]**. This protects the business from damage to its reputation and maintains customer trust **[An]**

Secondly, consistent high quality reduces the need for product recalls and refunds **[K]**. This saves the business money on replacement costs and administrative expenses **[An]**

Thirdly, maintaining quality standards ensures compliance with legal requirements and industry regulations **[K]**. This helps the business avoid fines, legal action and potential closure **[An]**

Finally, high quality maintenance supports employee morale and job satisfaction **[K]**. Workers take pride in producing quality products, leading to increased productivity and lower staff turnover **[An]**

> 
>   - To maintain customer satisfaction – so that customers continue to purchase and recommend the business to others
>   - To reduce costs associated with defects – which prevents waste and improves profit margins
>   - To meet legal and regulatory standards – avoiding penalties and maintaining operating licences
>   - To preserve brand reputation – ensuring long-term market position and competitive advantage
>   - To maintain employee pride and motivation – leading to better performance and reduced recruitment costs
>   - To ensure consistent performance – which builds reliability and customer confidence

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes.

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows.

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading.

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

**Appendix 2 **

**Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

**Appendix 3 **

**Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
|---|---|
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Explain the benefits and limitations of the following two ways of achieving quality production.

- Quality control
- Quality assurance

Which way should CC use? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Having inspectors check the mobile phone covers **[Ap]** at the end of production would catch faulty covers before they reach customers, protecting CC's reputation **[An]**. The ten production workers wouldn't need extra training, as inspectors would do the checking. However, quality control could increase costs for CC as they'd need to employ specialist inspectors **[An]**. If faulty covers are only found at the end, CC might waste materials and time making personalised products **[Ap]** they can't sell **[An]**

With quality assurance, problems could be spotted early, reducing waste and saving CC money in the long run **[An]**. It might also make workers feel more motivated, as they all have a responsibility for quality **[An]**. However, quality assurance would require training all ten workers **[Ap] **to check their own work, taking them away from production. Even after training, production of phone covers might slow down if workers are constantly checking for quality **[An]**

I recommend CC use quality assurance **[E]**. It may cost more to train workers initially, but should save money over time by reducing waste. Quality assurance fits well with CC's plan to make personalised covers **[Ap]**, as each stage of production for these unique items needs careful checking **[E]**. Quality control might lead to more wasted materials and time, which a new business **[Ap]** like CC can't afford **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Quality control**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Inspectors check each finished cover → stops faulty covers reaching customers
>     - Production workers need no extra training → only inspectors handle quality checks
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Hiring inspectors raises labour costs
>     - Finds faults only at the end → doesn’t show which step caused errors → waste from rework or scrapping
>     - Workers may feel less responsible for quality → careless mistakes may rise
> - **Quality assurance**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Workers check at every stage → catches faults immediately → fewer defects overall
>     - Cuts customer complaints and reduces scrap costs → preserves CC’s reputation for reliability
>     - Empowers staff → trusted to manage quality → often boosts motivation
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Training all ten line workers takes time and money
>     - Slows production as each step pauses for checks → may reduce output rate
>     - Requires consistent commitment from staff → lapses undermine the system
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Quality control is fastest to set up with minimal training but only fixes problems at the end and adds inspector wages
>   - Quality assurance prevents defects continuously, lowers waste and builds trust with customers yet needs investment in training and can slow production
>   - CC should weigh the importance of zero-defects and strong brand image against extra time and cost when deciding between these two methods

**The BB Health Spa (BB)**

Bethany owns The BB Health Spa in Main City in country X. Economic growth has been high for the last few years. The government of country X wants this growth to continue so it has reduced income tax. However, it is also worried about inflation becoming a problem so it has increased interest rates.

The BB Health Spa is very busy and Bethany is considering taking on a partner to help manage the business and give her more free time. However, she has been a sole trader for 10 years and wants the business to stay small.

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

**Appendix 1**

**Advert for treatments at The BB Health Spa**

**Appendix 2 **

**Weekly forecasts for two possible additional services**

|---|---|---|
| Additional customers | 200 | 50 |
|   |   |   |
| Average price charged per customer | \$5 | \$25 |
| Wages | \$60 | \$400 |
| Cost of sales | \$40 | \$125 |
| Lease of equipment | \$400 | \$175 |

**Appendix 3**

**Daily News **

**September**

**New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

There have been a number of changes in technology for health spas which allow the treatments to be much more effective in making skin look younger. Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

State the advantages and disadvantages of the following** three** ways to achieve good quality service at the health spa:

- only employ highly trained workers
- record all customer complaints
- buy only the best quality materials to use in the health spa.

Which do you think is the most important way? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Only employing highly trained workers would help ensure customers receive expert beauty treatments **[Ap]**, leading to higher satisfaction and the likelihood they will return in the future **[An]**. As Bethany already employs two qualified workers **[Ap]**, this approach aligns with her current practices. However, highly skilled staff expect to be well-paid, which could increase BB's costs **[An]**

Recording all customer complaints would help Bethany identify and address issues quickly, showing that Bethany cares about their experience **[An]**. For example, if clients complained about outdated equipment **[Ap]**, BB could consider upgrading. However, it's time-consuming and not all unhappy customers will provide feedback**, **so Bethany may not have the full picture to make important decisions **[An]**

Using only the best quality materials would help maintain BB's reputation for affordable yet effective treatments **[Ap]**. High-quality products could justify BB's prices **[An] **compared to nearby spas with newer equipment **[Ap]**. However, expensive materials might force Bethany to raise prices, potentially deterring price-sensitive customers **[An]**

The most important method is likely employing highly trained workers **[E]**. Skilled staff are crucial in a service-based business like BB. Even with top-quality materials, untrained workers could provide poor treatments, leading to customer dissatisfaction **[E]**. Highly trained staff can also help identify quality issues and suggest improvements, combining the benefits of the other two methods. This approach aligns with BB's current practice of using qualified workers **[Ap] **and Bethany's hands-on involvement in treatments, supporting the spa's reputation for quality at affordable prices **[E]**

**Protective Hats (PH)**

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for PH’s products**

PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work.

We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

High quality is guaranteed.

PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

**Appendix 2**

**Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director

From: Human Resources Director

Date: 1 October 2023

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

**Appendix 3 **

**PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

Consider the following** two** ways PH could ensure quality production.

- Quality control
- Quality assurance

Which way should PH choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Quality control could benefit PH by allowing end-of-process checks on their protective hats for construction sites, factories, and mines **[Ap]**. This method might be less expensive, which is important given PH's decreased profit margin **[An]** from 20% to 16% **[Ap]**. However, it could lead to more waste if faulty hats are rejected at the end of production, increasing costs **[An]**

Quality assurance aligns with PH's need for consistently high-quality safety equipment, with workers identifying and correcting issues at each stage. High quality output, delivered by all staff, could help PH maintain its market leader position **[Ap]** and support international expansion plans **[An]**. However, quality assurance would require employee training, slowing down production **[An]**

PH should choose quality assurance over quality control. While it may take time, it's better suited to maintaining the high standards required for safety equipment** [E]**. This method would help PH uphold its quality reputation **[Ap]**. Quality control, despite being cheaper and quicker to implement, doesn't offer the same level of consistency **[E]**, which is essential for a company producing safety-critical items for hazardous work environments **[Ap]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think quality control is the best method for a manufacturing business to use to achieve quality production? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Quality control tries to eliminate faults before products reach customers **[K]**, which helps maintain a business's reputation and reduces the likelihood of a business having to spend time dealing with the replacement of faulty items **[An]**

Another method is quality assurance. This stops errors before they happen by checking products throughout the process **[K]**. This means that partially complete products can be reworked when errors are identified, so fewer high-value finished items are rejected **[An]**

Quality control is not necessarily the best method for a manufacturing business to achieve quality production. Quality assurance is likely the better method in many instances **[E]**,** **because fewer mistakes mean fewer wasted resources, and the money saved should cover any additional training costs **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**

parts.problem_md: **Explain four** reasons why quality is important to a business.
parts.solution_md:
Quality helps attract and retain loyal customers **[K]**. When products meet or exceed customer expectations, they are more likely to make repeat purchases and recommend the business to others **[An]**

Secondly, high quality builds the reputation of the business or brand **[K]**. A strong reputation for quality can give a business a competitive advantage in the market **[An]**

Thirdly, maintaining quality reduces wastage and returns from unsatisfied customers **[K]**. This lowers costs for the business and improves profitability **[An]**

Finally, quality can be used as a unique selling point in promotional activities **[K]**. Businesses can differentiate themselves from competitors by emphasising their commitment to quality, which can help them expand into new markets **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Answers might include:
> 
>   - To establish a brand image – so that customers are encouraged to buy the product and new customers are attracted
>   - To build brand loyalty / customer loyalty – so that customers will make repeat purchases and maintain sales
>   - To maintain a good reputation / not to gain a bad reputation – friends and family tell others about the good or service which may lead to a good / bad reputation
>   - To increase sales / attract more customers – due to customer needs being satisfied by the products supplied
>   - So that faulty products do not have to be replaced – which would reduce waste / ensures customer safety / avoids legal action
>   - Able to charge a high price – may lead to higher profits / as may increase added value

parts.solution_md:
